guest.titre: Senior Vice President for Engineer Building Solutions
guest.bio_context: Rick Trammell has had an extensive career in HVAC and engineering, working for a very large HVAC manufacturer for many years before joining TACO almost 15 years ago. His primary focus at TACO is around custom engineered and designed and built skid packages. He leads the facility in Lubbock, Texas, which expanded from vertical turbine product fabrication to custom skid assembly for data center applications.

pending_qa.q: What energy efficiency innovations are data centers driving in HVAC and cooling equipment design?
pending_qa.r: Data centers are really focused on the cutting edge of cooling design and are looking to extract every bit of efficiency they can. They are constantly pushing the limits of energy and efficiency, including developing new air-cooled chiller designs and exploring how much energy can be saved or stored and what can be done with waste heat. This will advance the entire HVAC industry, as the cost-benefit for data centers makes efficiency improvements viable even when they might not have been before.

pending_qa.q: How does integrated skid design with coordinated components improve efficiency compared to picking individual pieces from different suppliers?
pending_qa.r: When equipment is no longer picked from different suppliers but instead coordinated as a package designed to work together, efficiency is maximized. The heat exchanger is picked to go with that specific pump and chiller for that exact design, making it hard to get much more efficient than that integrated systems approach.

pending_qa.q: What advice would Rick Trammell give to someone entering the rapidly evolving data center industry?
pending_qa.r: Rick Trammell recommends doing a lot of research, reading articles, and following relevant websites to stay informed and up to speed. He also suggests taking classes available in the data center space and getting involved in understanding the whole process, not just the specific part you work in, whether in racks or HVAC. The industry is evolving faster than you can keep up, so reading every article you can is essential, and the same applies to testing and trying out new technologies like AI.

pending_qa.q: Why was Lubbock, Texas selected as the location for TACO's custom skid manufacturing facility?
pending_qa.r: Lubbock became a natural next step because TACO already had a facility there doing fabrication work for vertical turbine products with welding experience and staff who had been in the business before. The location offered access to highly qualified welders, proximity to suppliers of materials needed, availability of space in the building with room for expansion, and the town and city have been very helpful in promoting and supporting the expansion.
